verdict.reasoning: Garvit's natural edge is his relatable, unapologetic Hinglish delivery and focus on economic relief for Indian creators/developers. However, competitors like Aryaman and Arshman generate massive authority by demonstrating tangible builds, systems, and case studies (e.g., Snitch, Comet, Claude Multi-Agent Systems). Combining Garvit's accessible tone and 'free hack' angle with structured competitor-grade workflows will create an unbeatable differentiator.
verdict.recommended_hook_structure: [Stop doing common expensive action / Bold contrarian claim] + [Specific Indian-relatable outcome or metric achieved in X time for free]. Example: 'Stop paying ₹2,000 for Claude every month. An Indian dev just made this open-source setup that gives you unlimited tokens.'
verdict.recommended_body_structure: Step 1: On-screen visual proof/demo ('Look here, see this screen...') -> Step 2: 3-part framework or system breakdown (Layer 1, 2, 3 or Tool + Backend + Prompt) -> Step 3: Emotional relief or business utility ('You don't need coding or cash to do this').
verdict.recommended_cta_structure: Comment '[SINGLE_RELEVANT_WORD]' and I'll DM you the complete step-by-step setup guide and free prompt template right now.
avoid_these: Avoid vague mindset advice without a direct hook to AI, business, or practical tools.
Avoid listing tools that sound fake or unverified without showing live on-screen UI proof.
Avoid passive endings; never end a video without an explicit comment keyword CTA for DM automation.
Avoid switching completely to academic English—the colloquial Hinglish inflection is essential for Indian audience retention.
